blocks.en: Consider that a conversation by telephone—when you are simply sitting by and not taking any part in that conversation—is one of the solemnest curiosities of modern life. Yesterday I was writing a deep article on a sublime philosophical subject while such a conversation was going on in the room. I notice that one can always write best when somebody is talking through a telephone close by. Well, the thing began in this way. A member of our household came in and asked me to have our house put into communication with Mr. Bagley's downtown. I have observed, in many cities, that the sex always shrink from calling up the central office themselves. I don't know why, but they do. So I touched the bell, and this talk ensued:
blocks.zh: 想象一下，电话交谈——当你只是坐在旁边，不参与任何谈话——是现代生活中最庄严的好奇心之一。昨天，当我在房间里进行这样的对话时，我正在写一篇关于崇高哲学主题的深入文章。我注意到，当有人在附近打电话时，一个人总是能写得最好。嗯，事情就这样开始了。我们家里的一位成员进来要求我让我们的房子与巴格利先生的市中心保持联系。我观察到，在许多城市，男性总是不敢亲自给中央办公室打电话。我不知道为什么，但他们就是这么做的。于是我按响了门铃，接下来就是这样的谈话：

blocks.en: Then I heard k-look, k-look, k'look—klook-klook-klook-look-look! then a horrible “gritting” of teeth, and finally a piping female voice: Y-e-s? (Rising inflection.) Did you wish to speak to me?
blocks.zh: 然后我听到k-look，k-look，k'look——klook-klook-klook-look-look！然后是可怕的“咬牙切齿”声，最后是尖锐的女声：是-是-是吗？ （语调上升）你想和我说话吗？
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: Without answering, I handed the telephone to the applicant, and sat down. Then followed that queerest of all the queer things in this world—a conversation with only one end to it. You hear questions asked; you don't hear the answer. You hear invitations given; you hear no thanks in return. You have listening pauses of dead silence, followed by apparently irrelevant and unjustifiable exclamations of glad surprise or sorrow or dismay. You can't make head or tail of the talk, because you never hear anything that the person at the other end of the wire says. Well, I heard the following remarkable series of observations, all from the one tongue, and all shouted—for you can't ever persuade the sex to speak gently into a telephone:
blocks.zh: 我没有回答，就把电话递给了应聘者，然后坐下来。接下来是这个世界上最奇怪的事情——一场只有一个结局的对话。你会听到有人提出问题；你听不到答案。你听到发出的邀请；你没有听到任何感谢的回报。你会听到死一般寂静的停顿，然后是明显不相干、毫无道理的惊呼、惊喜、悲伤或沮丧。你无法弄清楚谈话的要点，因为你永远听不到电话另一端的人说的任何话。好吧，我听到了以下一系列引人注目的观察结果，全部来自同一个舌头，而且全部都是喊叫的——因为你永远无法说服性别对着电话温柔地说：

blocks.en: A man delivers a single brutal “Good-by,” and that is the end of it. Not so with the gentle sex—I say it in their praise; they cannot abide abruptness.
